mainTopic: Is a שומר אבידה like a שומר חנם or a שומר שכר? רבה and רב יוסף test the question on several ברייתות, and אביי tests it on רבי יוחנן's ruling about כפל.
overview: Earlier on the daf, רבה holds that someone guarding a lost item he found is like a שומר חנם, who pays only for carelessness. רב יוסף holds he is like a שומר שכר, who also pays for theft and loss. רב יוסף challenges רבה from a ברייתא that makes the finder pay if the item is stolen or lost. רבה answers that this is about returning the item at midday, when the owner is not around, which counts as carelessness. A morning return frees the finder. רב יוסף then quotes the line 'he is always responsible.' רבה concedes that lost animals need extra guarding, but only animals. רבה next argues from ״הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם״ that the item may be returned to the owner's unguarded garden or ruin, which would fit a שומר חנם. רב יוסף answers that the garden is guarded, and the lesson is רבי אלעזר's rule that returning a lost item does not need the owner's knowledge. Finally אביי challenges רב יוסף from רבי יוחנן's ruling that a finder who falsely claims theft pays כפל. רב יוסף answers that the claim was about an armed bandit, who counts as a גנב because he hides from people. At the end of the amud, אביי begins a new challenge from a ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא: returning the item where the owner will see it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes the rest of a ברייתא. Once the finder puts the item back in a place where the owner will see it, he no longer has to deal with it. But if it was stolen or lost, he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he returned it to a place where the owner will see it, he no longer has to take care of it. If it was stolen or lost, he is responsible to pay for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that רב יוסף brings as a source for his view. This is the setup for the challenge against רבה that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes two rulings. First, putting the item back where the owner will see it ends the finder's duty to look after it. Second, if the item was stolen or lost, the finder is liable. The second ruling is what רב יוסף will build on, because liability for גניבה ואבידה is the mark of a שומר שכר.

keyTerms.meaning: To deal with it, to take care of it
It was stolen or it got lost
He is financially responsible for it, so he must pay
Someone guarding a lost item he found

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole debate turns on how to read the words "stolen or lost" in this ברייתא.

phrases.english: If he returned it to a place where he [the owner] will see it,
he is not obligated to deal with it.
If it was stolen or lost,
he is responsible for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that רב יוסף began quoting at the end of the previous daf.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that a שומר אבידה is like a שומר שכר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that makes the finder liable when the item is stolen or lost.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that a שומר אבידה is like a שומר חנם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes the finder liable when the item is stolen or lost. Liability for גניבה ואבידה is the mark of a שומר שכר, not a שומר חנם. The next step spells out this reading.

steps.title: Stolen or lost from the finder's own house?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks what "stolen or lost" means. Doesn't it mean the item was stolen or lost from the finder's house? If so, the finder pays for גניבה ואבידה, just like a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "stolen or lost" mean? Doesn't it mean it was stolen from his house or lost from his house?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף reads the ברייתא his way and uses that reading to challenge רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the item was stolen or lost while it was still in the finder's house. Then the finder is paying for ordinary גניבה ואבידה. Only a שומר שכר pays for that, which goes against רבה's view that a finder is a שומר חנם.

keyTerms.meaning: What, as in "what does it mean"
Isn't it? A word that suggests the answer is obviously yes
From his house

phrases.english: What is "stolen or lost"?
Is it not that it was stolen from his house
or lost from his house?
phrases.notes: "His house" means the finder's house, before he returned the item.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נִגְנְבָה אוֹ אָבְדָה לָאו נִגְנְבָה מִבֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that a שומר אבידה is like a שומר חנם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the finder pays for theft or loss from his own house, he has the liability of a שומר שכר, not a שומר חנם.

steps.title: No: stolen or lost from where he put it back
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the ברייתא means the item was stolen or lost from the spot where the finder returned it. Leaving it there is פשיעה, and even a שומר חנם pays for פשיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means stolen or lost from the place where he returned it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes away רב יוסף's reading by giving the words a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה moves the theft or loss from the finder's house to the spot where the finder left the item. Under this reading the finder pays for פשיעה, not for ordinary גניבה ואבידה. A שומר חנם is also liable for פשיעה, so the ברייתא fits רבה's view after all.

keyTerms.meaning: No, the start of a rejection
Negligence, which even a שומר חנם must pay for

phrases.english: No,
from the place where he returned it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא offered in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רב יוסף's reading of "stolen or lost", not the ברייתא itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא does not have to mean theft or loss from the finder's house. It can mean theft or loss from where he put the item back, which is פשיעה.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says he no longer has to deal with it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רבה's answer. The same ברייתא says that once the item is in that spot, the finder no longer has to deal with it. So leaving it there cannot be פשיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches: he is not obligated to deal with it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רבה's answer using the first part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said leaving the item at the return spot is פשיעה. But the ברייתא clearly says that once the finder puts it there, he no longer has any duty to look after it. If he has no duty, he was not careless, so the liability in the ברייתא must come from something else.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches! A phrase that introduces a challenge from the wording of a source

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new source. רב יוסף is turning the first line of the same ברייתא (step 1) against רבה's answer.

phrases.english: But it teaches:
he is not obligated to deal with it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָתָנֵי אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב לִיטַּפֵּל בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer in step 3 using the first line of the ברייתא from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the liability in the ברייתא is for פשיעה at the return spot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the finder has no further duty once the item is returned to that spot. With no duty, there can be no פשיעה, so רבה's reading does not work.

steps.title: רבה: the item was returned at midday
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the case where the finder pays is when he put the item back at midday, when the owner is not usually around.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: What case are we dealing with here? A case where he returned the item at midday.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers רב יוסף's challenge by narrowing the case where the finder pays to one where he returned the item at midday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף asked how leaving the item in the owner's spot could be פשיעה if the ברייתא says the finder is done once it is there. רבה answers that it depends on the time. At midday the owner is not around, so leaving the item then is careless, and even a שומר חנם pays for carelessness.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a formula that narrows a source to a specific case)
At midday
Carelessness. Even a שומר חנם pays for it.

phrases.english: He said to him:
With what are we dealing here?
Such as where he returned it at midday.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) by time of day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Returning the item to the owner's spot is always a proper return, so a loss from there cannot be פשיעה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A return at midday, when the owner is absent, is not a proper return. A loss after it counts as פשיעה.

steps.title: The ברייתא teaches two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the ברייתא describes two cases. A morning return frees the finder from responsibility. A midday return leaves him liable if the item is stolen or lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is teaching two cases, and this is how to read it. If he returned it in the morning to a place where the owner will see it, and the owner usually comes and goes and will see it, he no longer has to deal with it. If he returned it at midday to a place where the owner would see it, but the owner does not usually come and go then and will not see it, and it was stolen or lost, he is responsible for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה reads the whole ברייתא line by line to show how his answer fits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two lines of the ברייתא no longer contradict each other, because each one is about a different time of day. The morning line is the 'no longer has to deal with it' case. The midday line is the 'stolen or lost, he pays' case.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches two cases
In the morning
It is common that he comes in and goes out
He bears responsibility for it (must pay if it is lost)

steps.confusionAlert: The place is the same in both cases. It is a spot where the owner can see the item. The only difference is the time of day, which decides whether the owner will actually be there to see it.

phrases.english: And it teaches two cases,
and this is what it teaches:
if he returned it in the morning to a place where he will see it,
and it is common that he comes in and goes out and sees it,
he is not obligated to deal with it.
If he returned it at midday to a place where he will see it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא שְׁכִיחַ דְּעָיֵיל וְנָפֵיק, דְּלָא חָזֵי לַהּ;
phrases.english: since it is not common that he comes in and goes out, so he does not see it,
and it was stolen or lost,
he is responsible for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the answer in step 5 fits the full ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא into two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both lines of the ברייתא describe one case, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A morning return frees the finder. A midday return is פשיעה, so he pays.

steps.title: 'He is always responsible' suggests the finder is a שומר שכר
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes another line, 'he is always responsible until he returns it to the owner's property.' He argues that 'always' includes theft from the finder's own house, which would make the finder a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף challenged him: The ברייתא says, 'He is always responsible until he returns it to the owner's property.' What does 'always' add? Doesn't it mean even if it was stolen from his own house? Learn from this that a finder is like a שומר שכר!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a new challenge from another line of the ברייתא to prove his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'always' seems to add something beyond the careless case. The obvious addition is theft or loss from the finder's own house, where he did nothing wrong. Paying for that kind of loss is the rule of a שומר שכר, not a שומר חנם.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from a תנאי source)
Always
To his (the owner's) property
A paid watchman, who also pays for theft and loss

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is challenging רבה again.

phrases.english: He is always responsible,
until he returns it to his property.
What does 'always' mean?
Does it not mean even from his house?
Learn from this that he is like a paid watchman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new attack after רבה's answer in steps 5-6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's position that a finder is only a שומר חנם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Always' must cover loss even without carelessness, such as theft from his house. Paying for that is the liability of a שומר שכר.

steps.title: רבה agrees only for animals
steps.stepSummary: רבה concedes that for animals the finder is responsible like a שומר שכר. Animals that have already wandered off need extra guarding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: I agree with you about animals. Since they have gotten into the habit of wandering outside, they need extra guarding.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה partly agrees with רב יוסף, but limits that agreement to lost animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that already wandered off has shown it is likely to run away again. So the finder must guard it with extra care, like a שומר שכר. For ordinary objects that do not move by themselves, רבה keeps his view that the finder is only a שומר חנם.

keyTerms.meaning: I agree with you
Living creatures, animals
Walking outside (wandering off their usual path)
Extra guarding

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, a finder is normally a שומר חנם. He pays only for carelessness, such as returning the item at midday. Lost animals are the exception: they need extra guarding, so the finder is responsible for them like a שומר שכר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the finder's level of responsibility can depend on what kind of item was found. The basic category of the finder as a שומר חנם stays in place, with a special rule for animals.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I agree with you regarding animals,
because since they have taken to walking outside,
they need extra guarding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 by limiting it to animals.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial concession limited to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Always' proves that every finder is a שומר שכר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Always' refers to animals, which need extra guarding. Finders of other objects remain שומרי חנם.

steps.title: רבה quotes a ברייתא about returning to the garden or ruin
steps.stepSummary: רבה opens a challenge to רב יוסף by quoting a ברייתא. It learns from the doubled verb ״הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם״ that a lost item may be returned to any place belonging to the owner, including his garden or ruin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה challenged רב יוסף: "Return" teaches me only his house. From where do I know his garden and his ruin? The verse says "you shall return them," meaning to any place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה quotes a ברייתא to set up a challenge against רב יוסף. The challenge itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses the verb twice, ״הָשֵׁב״ and ״תְּשִׁיבֵם״. The first word teaches returning the item to the owner's house. The extra word stretches this to his garden and his ruin too. רבה will use these extra places to show how light the finder's duty is.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
"You shall surely return them" (דברים 22:1), with the verb doubled
Garden
A ruin, a broken-down or unused building on someone's property
The verse comes to teach

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection to Rav Yosef:
"Return" — I only know about [returning it] to his house;
phrases.notes: This is דברים 22:1, where the Torah says the verb twice: הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם.

phrases.english: to his garden and to his ruin, from where do we know?
The verse says "you shall return them": to any place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth over whether the finder is a שומר שכר, רבה now brings a new source to argue for his own view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's position that a finder carries the heavier responsibility of a שומר שכר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets the finder return the item to places beyond the house. The next step will argue that this means unguarded places.

steps.title: The garden must be unguarded, so the finder is like an unpaid guard
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks what kind of garden and ruin the ברייתא means. A guarded one would be the same as a house, so it must be unguarded. If leaving the item there is enough, the finder is like a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "to his garden and to his ruin" mean? If it means a guarded garden and a guarded ruin, that is the same as his house! So it must mean a garden and a ruin that are not guarded. Learn from this that a finder is like an unpaid guard!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה finishes his challenge. He shows the ברייתא must mean unguarded places, which proves the finder is only like an unpaid guard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the garden and ruin were guarded, the ברייתא would add nothing beyond "his house." So they must be unguarded, and the finder may still leave the item there and be free of it. That light level of care fits a שומר חנם, not a שומר שכר as רב יוסף holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarded, safely enclosed
That is the same thing, so why say it?
Learn from this, a conclusion drawn from the source
An unpaid guard, who is responsible only for carelessness

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבה is saying an unguarded garden is a safe place. His point is the opposite: the place is not safe, and the finder may still leave the item there. That shows how light his responsibility is.

phrases.english: What does "to his garden and to his ruin" mean?
If you say: to his garden that is guarded
and to his ruin that is guarded,
that is the same as his house!
Rather, it is obvious: to his garden that is not guarded
and to his ruin that is not guarded.
Learn from this: he is like an unpaid guard!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's view that a finder is a שומר שכר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A guarded garden would add nothing beyond the house, so the ברייתא must mean an unguarded one. Being allowed to leave the item somewhere unguarded shows only the light duty of a שומר חנם.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it is a guarded garden, and the point is that the owner need not know
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the ברייתא does mean a guarded garden and ruin. The new point is that the item counts as returned even if the owner does not know, following רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Really, it means a guarded garden and a guarded ruin. As for what bothers you, that this is the same as his house, this is what it teaches us: we do not need the owner's knowledge, like רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself. He keeps the guarded-garden reading and explains what it teaches that "his house" would not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה assumed a guarded garden adds nothing. רב יוסף says it adds something: the finder may leave the item in the owner's guarded garden or ruin without telling him, and it still counts as returned. So the ברייתא says nothing about unguarded places, and the proof that the finder is a שומר חנם falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually: keeping the first reading that was pushed aside
This is what it comes to teach us
The owner's knowledge or awareness
We do not need

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer moves the ברייתא's lesson from how much care the finder must take to whether the owner must know. That is how רב יוסף keeps his view that the finder is a שומר שכר.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף answering רבה.

phrases.english: Really, to his garden that is guarded
and to his ruin that is guarded;
and as for what is bothering you, "that is the same as his house":
this is what it teaches us:
that we do not need the owner's knowledge,
like Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers רבה's inference in step 10 by rejecting the claim that a guarded garden would add nothing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the ברייתא is teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A guarded garden adds nothing beyond the house, so the ברייתא must mean unguarded places.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means guarded places. It teaches that returning a lost item there works even without the owner's knowledge.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: returning a lost item does not need the owner's knowledge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר. Every return needs the owner's knowledge except returning a lost item, because the Torah's doubled wording included many ways of returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אלעזר said: Everyone needs the owner's knowledge, except for returning a lost item, because the Torah included many ways of returning in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר's rule, which רב יוסף relied on in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually someone giving back an item, such as a guard or a thief, must make sure the owner knows it was returned. A lost item is different, because the doubled ״הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם״ widens the ways of returning it. That is why leaving it in a guarded garden counts as returning it, even if the owner does not know.

keyTerms.meaning: Returning a lost item
The Torah included more, widening the law through extra wording
Many ways of returning

steps.whatToRemember: רבה tried to prove from ״הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם״ that a finder is a שומר חנם, since he may leave the item in an unguarded garden. רב יוסף answered that the garden is guarded. The lesson is רבי אלעזר's rule that returning a lost item does not need the owner's knowledge.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Elazar said:
Everyone needs the owner's knowledge,
except for returning a lost item,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי רִיבְּתָה בּוֹ תּוֹרָה הֲשָׁבוֹת הַרְבֵּה.
phrases.english: since the Torah included many ways of returning in it.
phrases.notes: This points back to the doubled הָשֵׁב תְּשִׁיבֵם, the verse quoted in step 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This quotes in full the rule of רבי אלעזר that רב יוסף mentioned in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Returning an item normally needs the owner's knowledge, but returning a lost item does not, because the Torah widened the ways of returning it.

steps.title: אביי challenges רב יוסף from the double payment rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites רבי יוחנן: a finder who falsely claims the lost item was stolen pays כפל. That only makes sense if the finder is a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Don't you agree that a finder is like an unpaid guard? רבי יוחנן said that a finder who falsely claims a thief took the item pays double. If he were a paid guard, why double? He should only have to pay back the item's value!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's view that a finder is a שומר שכר, using a ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A false claim is punished with כפל only when the lie would have gotten the guard off the hook. A theft claim frees a שומר חנם, but a שומר שכר must pay for theft anyway. So if רבי יוחנן gives a finder כפל for a theft claim, the finder must be a שומר חנם.

keyTerms.meaning: someone who is guarding a lost item he found
an unpaid guard. He is not responsible for theft or loss.
a paid guard. He is responsible for theft or loss.

steps.confusionAlert: The double payment is not a punishment for losing the item. It punishes the lie, and it applies only when the lie would actually have freed him from paying.

He should only need to pay the principal!
phrases.notes: A paid guard owes for theft anyway, so his lie gained him nothing. Without a gain, there is no double penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתְּ לָא תִּסְבְּרָא דְּשׁוֹמֵר אֲבֵידָה כְּשׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם דָּמֵי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף defended himself against the ברייתא, אביי brings a new challenge from רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's position that a שומר אבידה is a שומר שכר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כפל applies only when a false theft claim would have freed the guard. A theft claim frees only a שומר חנם, so רבי יוחנן's ruling implies the finder is a שומר חנם.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the finder claimed an armed bandit took it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that רבי יוחנן's case is a claim that an armed bandit took the item. Such a claim frees even a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Here we are dealing with a case where the finder claimed that an armed bandit took the item.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף keeps his view by reading רבי יוחנן's case as a claim about an armed bandit, not an ordinary thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An armed bandit counts as an unavoidable accident (אונס), and even a שומר שכר is not responsible for that. So this lie would have freed even a paid guard, and the כפל makes sense on רב יוסף's view.

keyTerms.meaning: "here, what case are we dealing with?" This phrase introduces a narrower reading of a source.
an armed bandit

phrases.english: He said to him:
Here, what are we dealing with?
A case where he claims that an armed bandit took it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by narrowing the case in רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was talking about a claim of an ordinary thief, which frees only a שומר חנם.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was talking about a claim of an armed bandit, which frees even a שומר שכר, so the finder can still be a שומר שכר.

steps.title: אביי: an armed bandit is a robber, not a thief
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that an armed bandit is a גזלן. A גזלן does not pay כפל, and רבי יוחנן spoke of a claim of a גנב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: An armed bandit is a robber!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כפל is a penalty only for a גנב, someone who steals in secret, not for a גזלן, who takes openly. An armed bandit takes openly by force. So a claim about him is not a 'thief claim,' and it should not lead to כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: a robber, someone who takes openly by force. He does not pay double.
a thief, someone who steals in secret. He pays double.

phrases.english: He said to him:
An armed bandit is a robber!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן's case is about an armed bandit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An armed bandit is a גזלן, and כפל applies only to a claim about a גנב. So the armed bandit reading does not fit רבי יוחנן's words or his ruling of כפל.

steps.title: רב יוסף: an armed bandit hides from people, so he is a thief
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that an armed bandit hides himself from people, so he has the status of a גנב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I say that an armed bandit, since he hides from people, is a thief.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his answer by explaining why an armed bandit counts as a גנב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What makes someone a גנב is that he hides from people. רב יוסף says an armed bandit also hides from people, so he counts as a גנב and not a גזלן. A claim about him is therefore a thief claim and carries כפל, and since such a claim frees even a שומר שכר (step 14), רב יוסף's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: hides himself
people

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף keeps his view that a finder is a שומר שכר. רבי יוחנן's double payment case is about a false claim that an armed bandit took the item. An armed bandit hides from people, so he counts as a גנב, and a paid guard is also freed by such a claim.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows what defines a גנב for the double payment: acting in hiding from people. That is why an armed bandit can count as a גנב and not a גזלן.

phrases.english: He said to him: For I say:
an armed bandit,
since he hides himself from people,
he is a thief.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: לִסְטִים מְזוּיָּין, כֵּיוָן דְּמִיטַּמַּר מֵאִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection in step 15 and closes this exchange.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the category: an armed bandit counts as a גנב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An armed bandit takes by force, so he is a גזלן and a claim about him carries no כפל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because he hides from people, an armed bandit has the status of a גנב, so the claim carries כפל and רב יוסף's view stands.

steps.title: אביי prepares to challenge רב יוסף from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי raises an objection to רב יוסף. The source he will use comes in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי raised an objection to him (רב יוסף):
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that אביי is about to challenge רב יוסף with a quoted source, and the source itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, אביי argued with רב יוסף from רבי יוחנן's ruling and from reasoning. Now he switches to quoting a ברייתא against רב יוסף's position. We can only judge how strong the challenge is once the ברייתא is quoted in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him. This word introduces a challenge based on a quoted source, usually a משנה or ברייתא.
A teaching from the time of the תנאים that is not in the משנה. The word אֵיתִיבֵיהּ usually leads into one.
The אמורא whose explanation of רבי יוחנן is being challenged here.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the challenge inside this word itself. אֵיתִיבֵיהּ only announces that a source is coming. The actual objection is in the next line.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is אביי and "him" is רב יוסף. The source he quotes comes right after this word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף answered that an armed bandit counts as a גנב, אביי now turns to a quoted source to challenge רב יוסף's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's explanation of רבי יוחנן: the claim was about an armed bandit, who counts as a גנב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A quoted ברייתא will be set against רב יוסף's position. The specific contradiction appears in the next step.
